holidays.name: National Google.com Day
holidays.description: A salute to the search engine that answers our questions, settles our debates and tells us whether that mole is worth worrying about. Celebrate by looking up something delightfully random, like how many penguins it takes to fill a bathtub.
holidays.origin: The observance marks September 15, 1997, the day the google.com domain name was registered. Google was later incorporated in 1998.
holidays.funFact: The name comes from 'googol', the number 1 followed by 100 zeros. The spelling is widely said to have been a typo when the domain was registered.

holidays.name: National Cheese Toast Day
holidays.description: A tribute to bread, cheese and a hot oven or skillet. It is the simplest comfort food around: melty, golden and crunchy. Pile on whatever cheese is in your fridge and call it dinner.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is a day for enjoying one of the humblest and most beloved snacks.
holidays.funFact: Cheese on toast has a long history in British cooking. The Welsh rarebit, a fancier cousin, was already being written about in the 1700s.

holidays.name: National Felt Hat Day
holidays.description: A day to dust off your fedora, trilby or bowler and wear it with style. Felt hats were the classic fall and winter headwear for generations.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits the old tradition of switching from summer straw hats to heavier felt ones in mid-September.
holidays.funFact: Felt is one of the oldest textiles in the world. It is made by matting and pressing fibers together rather than weaving them.
